corpus_row.citation: McReynolds L, O'Malley BW, Nisbet AD, Fothergill JE, Givol D, Fields S, Robertson M, Brownlee GG (1978) Sequence of chicken ovalbumin mRNA. Nature 273(5665):723-728. Claim supported: the ovalbumin mRNA encodes the 385-residue chicken egg-white protein ovalbumin, an ordinary hormonally regulated host gene product.
corpus_row.expected_class: not a TE - ordinary single-copy host protein-coding gene (ovalbumin, the archetypal serpin-family egg-white storage protein)
corpus_row.why_safe: Confusion axis: none at the domain level - this is the easy-case control that should never be called. Its only risk is generic ORF/repeat heuristics. Tool-independence: ovalbumin was characterised by direct protein and mRNA sequencing in 1978 and by complete chromosomal gene sequencing (Woo et al. 1981 Biochemistry 20:6437-6446), long predating any TE caller. Identity of THIS deposit was checked by derivation rather than taken on trust: CDS 27..1187 = 1161 nt = 386 codons + stop = 385 aa, matching mature chicken ovalbumin exactly. I deliberately chose this mRNA deposit over the classic genomic record J00895 (9206 bp) because CR1 non-LTR elements are documented in the chicken ovalbumin gene domain, so a genomic deposit could legitimately contain a TE inside its introns and would be an unsafe negative; an mRNA cannot. Bird taxon is absent from the existing negative panel.
